_schema: Ben's review queue. Canonical store; NEEDS_REVIEW.md is the readable mirror. Entry fields: id, title, raised (ISO date), kind, status, source, what, why_it_matters, options (array, only where there is a genuine fork), recommendation, files, resolution (null until Ben answers).
_note: Companion to backlog.json and review.json, NOT a replacement for either.
PURPOSE: things awaiting BEN'S JUDGEMENT. Three kinds live here:
- 'question'        â€” an open call nobody has made yet, usually surfaced by
doing adjacent work. Not blocking, or it would be a
backlog item with blocked_on set.
- 'decision-taken'  â€” a call made ON BEN'S BEHALF so work could continue.
Recorded here so it can be OVERTURNED rather than
quietly becoming precedent. This is the important half:
an unrecorded delegated decision is indistinguishable
from a decision Ben made.
- 'observation'     â€” something noticed in passing that is too small or too
cross-cutting to file, but which a human should see.
- 'novel-work'      â€” raised by a SESSION about its own task (Ben, 2026-08-20):
the work in hand feels NOVEL â€” no owning authority doc, no
saved role or established pattern fits, or it quietly grows
the project's scope. Raise it AT THE MOMENT the feeling
arises, then continue (or pause, if scope growth is large).
Gives Ben a drift detector: novelty should be chosen, not
accreted.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM review.json: review.json is a BLOCKER list â€” items blocked
on a visual artifact only Ben can produce (a mockup, an annotated screenshot).
Work there cannot proceed at all. Entries here are not blocking; they are
questions and reversible calls. If an entry turns out to need a mockup, move it
to review.json and leave a resolution here pointing at it.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM backlog.json: an entry here is not work. If Ben's answer
creates work, file a backlog item and resolve the entry with that item's id.
LIFECYCLE (revised 2026-08-14, Ben's ruling): this file is TRANSIENT â€” a live
queue of open calls, not a permanent audit trail. Append entries as they arise
and set status to 'resolved' with a resolution once answered, exactly as before.
But do NOT let resolved entries accumulate: prune them promptly rather than
holding them for posterity. The reasoning is not lost â€” it lands in code
comments, an authority doc, or a backlog item's design field at the moment the
work happens, and THAT is the durable record. Ben's own framing: 'the docs
should preserve changes made, and the review queue should only be for things
of that level of importance' â€” i.e. open and unresolved, not a history of
everything ever decided. A large housekeeping sweep this date closed 231
entries down to 2 genuinely open ones on this basis.

ARCHIVAL (2026-08-23): 'prune' now means MOVE, not delete. Run node tools/session/archive_reviews.js to move every resolved entry, verbatim, into docs/development/archive/needs-review-<quarter>.json, then re-render the mirror. The hot file holds open entries only.
SEEDED 2026-08-01 at Ben's request, populated from that session.

PURGE 2026-08-23: 240 open entries -> 18. Every entry referring only to backlog ids <= BL-568 (retired by the same-day backlog purge) was retired; 16 more were answered by reading the current docs and tree. All 223 are frozen verbatim in archive/needs-review-purged-2026-08-23.json, each with a resolution saying why. The survivors are asked as a form: tools/session/register/review_queue.js, built by register/build.js, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/53fb4e56-2eae-439e-bcb7-121fa49bd340 . NR-576 records the calls taken in the sweep.

DRAINED 2026-09-01 on Ben's instruction, from 117 open to 0. The queue had become a shadow backlog: most entries named WORK rather than a judgement, so ten backlog items (BL-713..BL-722) were minted to carry it and every entry was closed with a resolution saying where it went. THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT DRAINED, and it is now in CLAUDE.md Rule 0c: a call only Ben can make belongs here; work belongs in backlog.json; a fact worth remembering belongs in the comment or doc next to the code.

items.title: Two disclosure tensions the NR-1066 doc pass found
items.what: (1) A rival's treasury is private (Ben, 2026-10-26), but DISCOVERY.md § The operational fog says an open book shows "flows, balance", and FINANCE.md § Surfaces gives the Profitability ledger one row per nation, so a rival's filed return could expose its treasury. Whether a rival's return is readable at all is unruled. (2) The Industry lens, kept, weights rival plants by output_quantity, against "production stays private" (DISCOVERY.md; TOOLTIP.md). Also: the seat screen lists every major's treasury before play.
items.why_it_matters: Each decides what the player can see of a rival nation.
options: (1) A: a rival's return is unreadable; B: readable without its balance line. (2) A: the Industry lens shows rival plant count or presence, not output; B: output is public through the lens.
items.recommendation: (1) B; (2) A. The seat screen is a pre-play pick, so it may show treasuries.

items.title: Why are strategic nuclear weapons never fired, now there is no catastrophe?
items.what: Ben ruled tactical nuclear use permitted and strategic never fired (MILITARY.md § Missiles), the same day the Era catastrophe retired. The old reason - 'firing one is the catastrophe' - is gone. The rule stands as written, with the arsenal acting through Alarm alone.
items.why_it_matters: A rule with no stated cause reads as arbitrary to the player, and the AI needs to know what an arsenal is for.
options: A: keep the rule; the arsenal is pure deterrence through Alarm
B: allow strategic use with ruinous consequences (sentiment collapse with every nation, climate strain, the target razed)
C: strategic use only in answer to a strategic strike (second-strike only)
items.recommendation: A for v0.3.0: cheapest and legible; revisit B once war goals and peace exist.

items.title: Should a rival's unit counter show its HP and readiness?
items.what: The counter and the unit card show HP, readiness and morale for the player's own units only. A rival's counter shows its owner colour and unit count, and its card shows no condition bars. This follows BL-068 (a rival's internals stay private) as the battle card already applies it. Your brief said units show HP and readiness, without saying whose.
items.why_it_matters: Seeing a rival's spent units is how a player picks where to push, and fronts (BL-1427) will lean on it; but it is a widening of what the player sees of another nation, which is yours to rule.
options: C: a rival's bars only where the player has units in contact or a recon satellite overhead (the intelligence layer, BL-1431)
items.recommendation: C, with A until satellites exist: it makes intelligence a thing worth buying.

items.title: "Refit" now names two things
items.what: MILITARY.md § Land — equipment, refit and manpower already uses "refit" for refilling a wounded unit's HP. The new verb uses it for changing a unit's type. The doc says they are distinct, but GLOSSARY.md settles neither.
items.why_it_matters: One word for two mechanics confuses the player and the action dictionary.
options: A: "Refit" is the type change; the HP refill becomes "Replenish"
B: keep "Refit" for HP; the type change becomes "Upgrade"
items.recommendation: A. The button on the unit card already reads Refit, and replenish is the military term for refilling men and kit.

items.title: A retired recipe slot is a new pattern
items.what: Recipe ids are list positions saved in every building, so the five capacity-yard recipes cannot be deleted. They stay in recipes.lua with retired = true and no inputs or outputs; the loader refuses a retired recipe that names any; a building running one idles but still pays wages. The capacity resource keeps its enum slot, price and spoilage so old stock decays.
items.why_it_matters: No doc owns retiring a recipe; the next retirement will copy this.
options: A: write the pattern into PRODUCTION.md as the rule
B: also demolish or refund retired-recipe buildings on load
items.recommendation: A now; B only if old saves matter before v1.0.

items.title: A front key may now sit across the border
items.source: Lane F report, sprint 61 (BL-1441 front edge cases), 2026-10-31
items.what: A span whose every tile an earlier span already claimed used to be dropped, leaving a front unnamed. It is now keyed by the lowest unclaimed tile on the neighbour's side. The lane wrote the rule into MILITARY.md § Fronts. Rival front assignment also now skips a front no march can reach (front_reachable); a player-assigned unit with a refused march is still re-issued each tick.
items.why_it_matters: An authority-doc rule changed inside a defect fix. Digests did not move.
items.recommendation: Accept; the key is an identity, not a place.

items.title: State port siting has no doc home
items.source: Lane G report, sprint 61 (BL-1420 lane and port defects), 2026-10-31
items.what: A coastal capital's state port sits on the coastal tile nearest the capital, a rule stated only in a code comment. On seed 40 that tile lay in a sea pocket joined to open water only across a hex diagonal, which the four-step lane walk cannot cross, so no lane left it. The lane added a preference for open sea (the largest four-connected piece of the six-connected sea) in code only.
items.why_it_matters: A generation rule with no authority doc. It moves D_land on every seed with such a pocket.
items.recommendation: Write the siting rule, open sea included, into LOGISTICS.md § 4b beside the harbour rules.

items.title: Alarm's new vocabulary: five factors, three modifier subjects
items.source: Lane S report, sprint 61 (BL-1458 sentiment emitters, BL-1432 Alarm as sentiment), 2026-10-31
items.what: To make Alarm's RELATIONS § 6 causes emit, the lane added five sentiment factors (technology_visible, facility_visible, border_force, trade_severed, unrest_visible authored zero), three modifier subjects on the meta layer (alarm_toward multiply, alarm_tell add in points, alarm_decay multiply) read by nation_tech.cpp, and widened the tech-store audit grammar (a points subject; "N% faster" reads as +N). A large facility is a state asset costing at least 450 (launchpad, airbase; not the university). 14 Digitisation effect rows now write Alarm; six stay unread (no Nuclear Plant, no accord-partner store, "spike" and "drift" ambiguous, no capability-only scale, no world-wide decay scale).
items.why_it_matters: New META_LAYER vocabulary and five enumerators no doc named. The emitter module sentiment_emitters.cpp has no owning doc section beyond RELATIONS § Who emits.
items.recommendation: Accept; write the five factors into RELATIONS § Who emits and the three subjects into META_LAYER at merge.

items.title: Major opening kit: most processor slots fail Pass 3, and majors run near break-even
items.source: BL-1473 lane, branch worktree-agent-a1fb67f8f6d2e0152 at 14aefef5; quick-tier census 2026-11-03
items.what: Quick tier (seeds 0, 28, 46, 12; 20:4; 20 quarters). Parity improves: treasury spread median 21x -> 2.0x (Standard) / 1.7x (Rich-core); buildings 13x -> 2.3x. Workability falls: Standard median net +1 per quarter, 8 of 16 majors losing money (baseline median +910, about a quarter losing); Rich-core median +255, 6 of 16 losing, none broke. Cause: kit processors fail Pass 3. Steel, refined fuel and power fail the want bound, which is body-wide, so the minors' walk already covers them; food rations, refined copper and machinery fail spare input, since one extractor per raw does not cover a plant at t_idle. Standard places a median of about 2-3 of its 6 processors. Also unbuilt: the logistics slots, so majors keep 2-47 nodes and their bills.
items.why_it_matters: The doc says each kit processor runs on day one; on these seeds it mostly does not stand. The kit is not merged to main until this is decided.
options: Exempt kit processors from the want bound (keep chain-feasible and sized)
Read want at the major's own markets rather than the body
Size kit extraction to its processors (enough feed for each slot)
Build the logistics slot cap as the doc says
items.recommendation: The first and third together, then the fourth; re-run the census on both kits.

items.title: Novel seam: generation helpers exposed through corporation_generation_detail.hpp
items.what: The kit reuses Pass 3 helpers, so they moved from an anonymous namespace into namespace corpgen behind a new detail header. No doc owns that seam.
items.why_it_matters: It lets other TUs call generation internals directly.
items.recommendation: Accept as the kit's seam; note it in CORPORATION_GENERATION.md if kept.

items.title: Kit logistics cap: hubs stacked at the capital stay outside the two hub slots
items.what: The cap counts every node on the capital tile as the capital's source, outside the slots, and stack_logistics_hubs may still stack hubs at a capped major's capital. Kept that way: stacked capital hubs are read as the source's capacity (the doc's "4 + the source"), so the cap bounds the network's reach, not the capital's throughput.
items.why_it_matters: A major can carry more than two hubs' bill if its capital stacks. Counting them against the slots would bound the bill but could starve the capital's Logistic Points.
items.recommendation: Keep; revisit if the census shows capital stacks driving a major's bill.

items.title: Rival embargo bars and the offer cooldown: calls taken in the relations lane
items.what: (1) Embargo enacts above utility 0.20 and repeals below 0.10 - no range was ruled; at 0.30 no rival ever embargoed (0.10: 713 pair-ticks, 0.20: 38, 0.30: 4). Census: 3 enacted, 3 repealed, none on the player. (2) The 4-tick peace-offer cooldown sits in offer_peace itself, so it binds the player too; the ledger disables Offer peace and names the quarters left. (3) War dispatches post to Field with no speaker.
items.why_it_matters: An embargo can prop itself up: it cuts the target's cargo, which removes the author's trade-exposure cost and raises its own Alarm through trade_severed, until decay lifts it. All three census embargoes still lifted.
items.recommendation: Keep all three; revisit the bars if embargoes stop lifting once Trust can fall further (NR-1129).

items.title: Rivals fortify any border-province tile their units stand on
items.what: 'Widen to border posts' was read as any of the rival's own tiles with its units on them, in a province that holds a tile of a hostile front - so a garrison posted inside a border province is fortified where it stands. Written into AI_OPPONENT.md § 11's bunker entry as the ruling's widening. Rival bunkers over 16 seeds: 1 -> 15 (13 completed); none for the player.
items.why_it_matters: Narrower reading (garrison post tiles only) would build fewer. The roughly 15x bunker spend moved seed 46's G1t50 85.7 -> 83.1.

items.title: Kit: a major's kept foundings no longer refund into the flat treasury
items.what: The opening reserve refunded founding payments (state plants, ports) a major made from its history chest. With the flat treasury replacing that chest, every founding of a major is zeroed, kept or removed, so the reserve refunds nothing and every major enters the settle at exactly the kit treasury (seed 0: 1,442 credits of refunds gone on Rich-core). The brief named only removed foundings.
items.why_it_matters: Without it a major that founded a kept port opens above the flat figure.

items.title: Kit: refined fuel, power and ordnance slots are never wanted, so they substitute
items.what: On every major the refined fuel, power and (Rich-core) ordnance slots fail the want bound and fall down the ladder to another processor. Nothing generation reads draws refined fuel; power want is per grid and grids read as fed; units' ordnance draw is not in the want reading. The doc says each kit processor runs on day one; these three never stand as named.
items.why_it_matters: The kit's named energy and military-supply lines are absent from every major's opening; the slots become other plants.
options: Count those real draws in the want reading (building fuel upkeep, unit ordnance, grid need)
Replace the three slots in the kit with goods that are wanted
items.recommendation: Count the real draws: the goods are wanted in play, and generation is blind to it.

items.title: Build times anchored at x2/3, so a mine takes 120 days
items.what: Ben chose "scale all down, keep the differences" without naming the anchor. Taken: extraction 180 to 120, the rest x2/3: bunker 60, processing 180, base 240, university 300, launchpad 360.
items.why_it_matters: A processor at 120 instead would mean x4/9 and much faster builds overall.

items.title: Occupation defaults
items.what: Taken: an empty tile is occupied on entry, with no stay needed; an occupied tile's output is denied to its owner and not gained by the occupier; occupation needs a war, in Ben's words "when at war", while push stays open under one-way hostility and without a war still stops at the first tile. Rivals' pushes take ground under the same rule with no new grant, since push is an existing verb.
items.why_it_matters: Sets how fast wars move the map. Hostility without war taking no ground is the reading to confirm; the rival reading is the one to check against the AI register.

items.title: A convoy with no way round
items.what: Ben chose re-route. Taken for the case with no route: dispatch refused with a surfaced reason; in-flight cargo returns to origin. A neutral third nation is not bound by the front.
items.why_it_matters: Returning cargo is not captured, so war does not seize goods; capture was the other option on the form.

items.title: "Same amount" read as same at the handoff
items.what: Today majors share 12,000 before the settle and reach 16,994-36,214 when play starts. Taken: one figure set at the handoff, after the settle.
items.why_it_matters: Setting a value after the settle could read as a clamp; it is written as the kit's grant.

items.title: Small defaults on the UI list
items.what: Taken, stated to Ben before the form: scrub stays round; rail Track reads Railroad; drag-select is own units with shift to add; trades gate on the viewed market only; alerts are not dismissable; the side-by-side nation scan goes.
items.why_it_matters: Each is a one-line reversal if he disagrees.

items.title: Schooling and University are not in the Build door
items.what: Read from selection_panel.cpp:4764: the door lists Port, Marketplace, Launchpad, Hub and Station under Infrastructure, Base, Airbase, Bunker and Research Institute under Military, and no Schooling or University. The form did not ask.
items.why_it_matters: If unintended, players cannot build them, and Research Institute under Military reads oddly. Fold them into the construction pass, or leave?

items.title: What 96 px does beyond the top rung
items.what: Ben ruled the master at 96 px and the top rung lowered to about 96 px. Written beyond that: the lower zoom rungs halve from about 96; and a 4K-height window now magnifies the top rung about 2x (computed), where the 2026-10-10 ruling accepted about 1.7x. TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md keeps a benchmark measured at 128 px, labelled as such.
items.why_it_matters: Halving lowers every zoom level, not only the closest, and 4K play looks softer than the accepted figure.

items.title: Research spends outside net: should it count, and how does it share with construction?
items.what: The research line takes a weighted share of the treasury, up to what the queue owes, as a direct expenditure the quarterly return does not carry. Mean 1,644 credits a major-quarter over 20 years, against net of 1,000-2,500. So the header NET and the Earnings chart overstate free cash, and "a mine costs six months of net" means different things before and after research. Recommended: book research in the return, so NET is the money left; the mine target then reads net after research.
items.why_it_matters: A player with a research queue may have little left for construction under the new prices, and a share of treasury shrinks as the opening treasury falls. This sets how research and construction compete at the opening.
items.resolution: Ben: "Yes, count research." Research counts inside net; written into FINANCE § The quarterly return; the work is BL-1539 (research in return).
